title: Synthetic DisputeFlow demonstration policy (not PayPal terms)

sections.title: Scope and synthetic policy disclosure
sections.text: This document is a synthetic DisputeFlow demonstration policy. It is not a PayPal agreement, seller protection policy, buyer protection policy, or legal interpretation. Its invented rules demonstrate auditable non-monotonic reasoning only.

children.title: Buyer nonreceipt recommendation
children.text: In this synthetic demo, a verified claim_nonreceipt fact normally supports decision_accept_claim. A stronger applicable contrary rule can defeat this recommendation.

children.title: Verified delivery exception
children.text: In this synthetic demo, a verified delivery_verified fact normally supports the explicit opposite of decision_accept_claim, unless tracking_invalid is established.

children.title: Invalid tracking defeater
children.text: In this synthetic demo, established tracking_invalid is a defeater protecting decision_accept_claim from contrary delivery-based rules. This exception alone does not establish decision_accept_claim.

children.title: Delivery rule overrides nonreceipt rule
children.text: In this synthetic demo, seller_delivery has higher priority than buyer_nonreceipt. This priority only matters when both rules are applicable and their conclusions conflict.

children.title: Invalid tracking defeater overrides delivery rule
children.text: In this synthetic demo, the invalid_tracking defeater has higher priority than seller_delivery.

children.title: Buyer quality complaint
children.text: In this synthetic demo, a verified quality_complaint fact normally supports decision_accept_claim.

children.title: Competing seller inspection
children.text: In this synthetic demo, a verified seller_inspection fact normally supports the explicit opposite of decision_accept_claim. No priority between buyer_quality and seller_quality is specified; competing extensions require governance.

sections.title: Merchant evidence submission mapping
sections.text: In this synthetic demo, the explicit opposite of decision_accept_claim strictly implies decision_provide_evidence. The merchant can submit evidence to PayPal; this does not adjudicate the dispute or deny a buyer claim.
